hypothesis: Residual prediction in tendency-normalized output units, with capped fixed tendency loss, reduces temperature/salinity imprinting while retaining physical variability and velocity skill over long rollouts.
resolution: 1 degree; validate the production U-Net and long rollouts before a separate quarter-degree confirmation

statistics.mask: land counted as zero change; average over the full grid
statistics.new_copy: checksum-verified copy in this run's immutable submission bundle

model.baseline: Paper Samudra 2 widened modified ConvNeXt U-Net, batch normalization, float32
model.residual_output_scale: physical persistence RMS / state standard deviation, saved as a fixed model buffer

training.walltime: 24 hours with checkpoint resume on Slurm requeue

variance maps and global mean trajectories
analysis.interpretation: This extends the report's small-CNN one-step evidence to a production U-Net and long rollouts. The joint parameterization and horizon changes do not identify loss-only causality. Quarter-degree confirmation is a subsequent experiment.
